mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate level is inversely related to S&P 500 20-day returns, so a low rate (current value 1.55%) predicts positive returns. A lower rate reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, increasing the present value of future cash flows and driving equity prices higher.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 2.0% and 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases, or the rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 259.0 (current value 258.82) signals accelerating inflation, which typically leads to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 20-day returns as investors price in higher future interest rates and reduced real earnings growth.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 259.0 and 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 3.8% and decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 152000.0 (current values: UNRATE=3.6, PAYEMS=152186.0) indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a recession and causes negative S&P 500 20-day returns as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 3.8 and PAYEMS < 152000.0 and 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (GDP growth above 2.0% and unemployment below 4.0%), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1600.0 (current value 1608.0) signals a weakening housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 20-day returns as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: GDPC1 > 19200.0 and UNRATE < 4.0 and HOUST < 1600.0 and 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of residential sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand and economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 20-day returns as investors anticipate higher corporate earnings and reduced risk aversion. Current RSAFS value is 529766.0, which is above the threshold of 530000.0 for the signal.
failure_condition: RSAFS > 530000.0 and 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases, or the rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 108.0 (current value 109.2026) signals a weakening manufacturing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 20-day returns as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings and economic contraction.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 108.0 and 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 259.0) and a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1.6%) signals a 'stagflation' risk, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 20-day returns as investors fear both inflation and economic stagnation. Current values: CPIAUCSL=258.82, FEDFUNDS=1.55.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 259.0 and FEDFUNDS < 1.6% and 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 3.8% (current value 3.6%) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 60-day returns as investors react to the negative economic signal.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 3.8 and 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
